blocks.text: VOCs are a large group of organic compounds that evaporate easily at room temperature and are emitted as gases from certain solids or liquids. Liquid fuels are major sources affecting outdoor air; vehicle exhaust and the burning of liquid fossil fuels, wood and garbage all release VOCs. Short-term exposure causes eye, nose and throat irritation, headache and nausea; long-term exposure damages the liver, kidneys and central nervous system. They contribute to both indoor and outdoor pollution; common VOCs are benzene, xylene, toluene, ethanol, formaldehyde and acetone.

blocks.prompt: How do VOCs affect air quality (Quick Check 14.2c)?
blocks.explanation: They evaporate from fuels, solvents and burning wood or garbage into the air, where they irritate eyes and airways directly and, with nitrogen oxides in sunlight, form the ozone and PAN of photochemical smog; long exposure harms the liver, kidneys and nervous system.

items: VOCs evaporate easily (benzene, xylene, toluene, ethanol, formaldehyde, acetone) from fuels, exhausts, wood and garbage; irritation and nausea short-term, liver, kidney and nervous damage long-term; indoor and outdoor pollution.
